statements.statement: The letter 'k' is always silent when it comes before 'n' at the beginning of a word.
statements.statement_uz: 'K' harfi so'z boshida 'n' dan oldin kelganda doim jim.
statements.explanation: Examples: 'know', 'knife', 'knee', 'knight' - the 'k' is silent.

statements.statement: 'Through', 'though', and 'thought' all rhyme with each other.
statements.statement_uz: 'Through', 'though' va 'thought' bir-biriga qofiyalanadi.
statements.explanation: through /θruː/, though /ðəʊ/, thought /θɔːt/ - all different pronunciations.
statements.explanation_uz: through /θruː/, though /ðəʊ/, thought /θɔːt/ - barchasi turli talaffuz.

statements.statement: The 'gh' in 'ghost' is pronounced differently from the 'gh' in 'laugh'.
statements.statement_uz: 'Ghost' dagi 'gh' 'laugh' dagi 'gh' dan farqli talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: 'Ghost': 'gh' = /g/ sound. 'Laugh': 'gh' = /f/ sound.

statements.statement: The word 'Wednesday' is pronounced exactly as it is spelled.
statements.statement_uz: 'Wednesday' so'zi yozilganidek talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: 'Wednesday' is pronounced /ˈwenzdeɪ/ - the first 'd' is silent.

statements.statement: The 'th' sound in 'the' is the same as the 'th' sound in 'think'.
statements.statement_uz: 'The' dagi 'th' tovushi 'think' dagi 'th' tovushi bilan bir xil.
statements.explanation: 'The' has voiced /ð/. 'Think' has voiceless /θ/. Feel your throat vibrate for 'the'.
statements.explanation_uz: 'The' jarangli /ð/. 'Think' jarangsiz /θ/. 'The' uchun tomoqingiz tebranishini his qiling.

statements.statement: The word 'colonel' is pronounced 'KOL-o-nel'.
statements.statement_uz: 'Colonel' so'zi 'KOL-o-nel' talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: 'Colonel' is pronounced /ˈkɜːrnl/ ('KER-nl'), similar to 'kernel'.

statements.statement: Silent 'e' at the end of a word usually makes the previous vowel long.
statements.statement_uz: So'z oxiridagi jim 'e' odatda oldingi unlini uzun qiladi.
statements.explanation: Compare: 'bit' vs 'bite', 'not' vs 'note', 'cut' vs 'cute'.

statements.statement: 'Read' (present) and 'read' (past) are pronounced the same way.
statements.statement_uz: 'Read' (hozirgi) va 'read' (o'tgan) bir xil talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: Present 'read' rhymes with 'need'. Past 'read' rhymes with 'red'.
statements.explanation_uz: Hozirgi 'read' 'need' bilan qofiyalanadi. O'tgan 'read' 'red' bilan qofiyalanadi.

statements.statement: The word 'queue' has 4 silent letters.
statements.statement_uz: 'Queue' so'zida 4 ta jim harf bor.
statements.explanation: 'Queue' is pronounced /kjuː/. Only 'q' and 'u' (as /kj/) are heard; 'e', 'u', 'e' are silent.
statements.explanation_uz: 'Queue' /kjuː/ talaffuz qilinadi. Faqat 'q' va 'u' (/kj/ sifatida) eshitiladi; 'e', 'u', 'e' jim.

statements.statement: 'Island' contains a silent 's'.
statements.statement_uz: 'Island' da jim 's' bor.
statements.explanation: 'Island' is pronounced /ˈaɪlənd/ - no 's' sound.

statements.statement: All words ending in '-tion' are pronounced with a 'shun' sound.
statements.statement_uz: '-tion' bilan tugaydigan barcha so'zlar 'shun' tovushi bilan talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: '-tion' is always /ʃən/: nation, station, education, information.

statements.statement: The 'b' in 'doubt' and 'debt' is pronounced.
statements.statement_uz: 'Doubt' va 'debt' dagi 'b' talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: The 'b' is silent in both words: /daʊt/, /det/.

statements.statement: 'Woman' and 'women' have different vowel sounds in the first syllable.
statements.statement_uz: 'Woman' va 'women' birinchi bo'g'inda turli unli tovushlariga ega.
statements.explanation: 'Woman' /ˈwʊmən/, 'women' /ˈwɪmɪn/ - different first vowels.

statements.statement: The word 'comfortable' has 4 syllables when pronounced correctly.
statements.statement_uz: 'Comfortable' so'zi to'g'ri talaffuz qilinganda 4 ta bo'g'inga ega.
statements.explanation: Most native speakers say 3 syllables: 'COMF-ter-bl' /ˈkʌmftəbl/.
statements.explanation_uz: Ko'pchilik ona tilida so'zlovchilar 3 bo'g'in deyishadi: 'COMF-ter-bl' /ˈkʌmftəbl/.

statements.statement: 'Clothes' and 'close' are pronounced exactly the same.
statements.statement_uz: 'Clothes' va 'close' aynan bir xil talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: Both are pronounced /kləʊz/ in casual speech, though 'clothes' can be /kləʊðz/.
statements.explanation_uz: Ikkalasi ham oddiy nutqda /kləʊz/ talaffuz qilinadi, garchi 'clothes' /kləʊðz/ bo'lishi mumkin.

statements.statement: The 'ough' combination has only one pronunciation in English.
statements.statement_uz: 'Ough' kombinatsiyasi ingliz tilida faqat bitta talaffuzga ega.
statements.explanation: 'ough' has many sounds: through /uː/, though /əʊ/, tough /ʌf/, thought /ɔː/, cough /ɒf/.
statements.explanation_uz: 'ough' ko'p tovushlarga ega: through /uː/, though /əʊ/, tough /ʌf/, thought /ɔː/, cough /ɒf/.

statements.statement: The word 'schedule' is pronounced the same in British and American English.
statements.statement_uz: 'Schedule' so'zi Britaniya va Amerika ingliz tilida bir xil talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: British: /ˈʃedjuːl/ (SHED-yool). American: /ˈskedʒuːl/ (SKEJ-ool).

statements.statement: The letter 'h' is always pronounced at the beginning of words.
statements.statement_uz: 'H' harfi doim so'z boshida talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: Silent 'h': hour, honest, heir, honor. The 'h' is not pronounced.
statements.explanation_uz: Jim 'h': hour, honest, heir, honor. 'h' talaffuz qilinmaydi.

statements.statement: 'Their', 'there', and 'they're' are all pronounced differently.
statements.statement_uz: 'Their', 'there' va 'they're' barchasi turlicha talaffuz qilinadi.
statements.explanation: All three are homophones, pronounced /ðeər/.

statements.statement: The word 'subtle' has a silent 'b'.
statements.statement_uz: 'Subtle' so'zida jim 'b' bor.
statements.explanation: 'Subtle' is pronounced /ˈsʌtl/ - the 'b' is silent.
